assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson closed the Standard Model and is a discovery at the centre of fundamental physics, with exceptionally clear and lasting impact. The theoretical prediction was recognised in 2013; the experimental discovery, which required two decades of detector and analysis work, is the natural complement.
assessment.attribution: Credit rests on the leadership of the two experiments. Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of the announcement, Jenni was a founding figure of ATLAS, and Virdee a founding figure of CMS, so the trio covers both collaborations. Della Negra is an equally defensible CMS founder, so the choice is a real compromise, and the collaboration-wide character of the result strains the three-person rule.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: independently confirmed by two experiments, with coupling measurements that have grown stronger through Run 2 and Run 3. Recognition is timely, even somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Which three of the four credited people best represent a collaboration-scale discovery is contested.
I rely on my own recollection of the specific roles held at the time of the 2012 announcement and have not verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned the cosmic microwave background into a precision tool and fixed the age, geometry and composition of the universe, establishing the concordance cosmology with high accuracy. For a theorist concerned with dark energy and early-universe physics, these measurements are the empirical anchor.
assessment.attribution: Bennett was the principal investigator and Page and Spergel were central to the instrument and the cosmological analysis, which makes a coherent trio. Other WMAP team members and the COBE and Planck lineages complicate the picture but do not displace this group.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, independently confirmed and refined by Planck and ground-based CMB experiments. The 2006 prize to COBE and the 2019 prize to Peebles have recognised neighbouring work, so overlap with earlier prizes is a consideration.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views WMAP as sufficiently distinct from the COBE prize and from Planck.
Relative weighting of the instrument builders against the analysis team is a matter of judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the identification of a first source in the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy as a new window. This is a clear and original discovery, delivered by a very large and ambitious instrument.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the leading figure behind the IceCube concept and programme, Spiering was a long-time spokesperson and an early driver of the field, and Karle contributed decisively to detector design and the array's construction and operation. The credited trio is plausible for a collaboration-scale result.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well established and has been supported by multiple analyses. Source identification is still developing, and the larger interpretation remains open, though the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: Whether the sources of the bulk of the flux are understood well enough for the committee to be comfortable.
KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD contributions, and the question of whether Antarctic neutrino-detector precursors such as AMANDA deserve explicit credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators created a new class of matter, with a theoretical prediction followed by a rapid experimental realisation, and a wide influence on condensed-matter physics. The link between prediction and observation is unusually clean.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theoretical foundation, Molenkamp observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, and Hasan realised the three-dimensional materials. The selected trio covers theory, 2D experiment and 3D experiment, but the omission of Mele and of the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposal is an unresolved allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently across many materials and laboratories. The field is mature, though the practical payoff has been slower than hoped.
uncertainties: Credit division between Kane and Mele, and the role of the HgTe prediction, is disputed.
Priority questions among the early 3D topological-insulator experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea, reached fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 and now serve as probes of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and possible dark-sector physics. The invention is clear, original and of lasting use in precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept and Ye brought the clocks to record accuracy. This is a natural two-person pairing, although the 2005 prize to Hall and Hänsch on frequency combs and the ion-clock work of Wineland already cover related ground.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced in several laboratories, with active work toward a redefinition of the second.
uncertainties: Whether optical clocks are viewed as distinct from earlier prizes on frequency combs and ion control.
Contributions of other groups to the clock development, for example Lemonde and Gill, are not captured in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background is a new observational window and potentially probes supermassive black-hole binaries or exotic early-universe physics. The scientific stakes for fundamental physics are high.
assessment.attribution: The result is a product of several large collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA) and attributing it to three people is difficult. McLaughlin and Siemens are NANOGrav leaders and Kramer is a leading figure in the European array, but other leaders, and the earlier theory of Hellings and Downs and of Detweiler, are not covered.
assessment.maturity: Premature. The significance of the Hellings-Downs correlation is evidence-level rather than a decisive detection, and the origin of the signal, supermassive binaries or new physics, is unresolved.
uncertainties: Whether the signal will reach firm detection significance and what its source is.
A fair division of credit across competing collaborations and pulsar-timing pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The images of the shadows of M87* and Sgr A* provide direct visual evidence of horizon-scale strong-field gravity and a striking, clear test of general relativity. The result is appealing both scientifically and to the public, and is relevant to my own field of black-hole physics.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the VLBI development and the collaboration, and Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept. The enterprise is collaboration-wide, and Narayan's theoretical modelling is also credited, so the allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Two source images exist and the interpretation of the ring as a shadow is broadly accepted, but the tests of general relativity are still limited in precision and interpretation depends on modelling of the accretion flow. The result is moderately mature but recognition may be a few years early.
uncertainties: How far the images constrain alternatives to general-relativity black holes.
Strong collaboration character of the discovery makes a three-person limit contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cold-dark-matter paradigm of hierarchical structure formation is the foundation of modern cosmological structure theory and explains the large-scale distribution of galaxies. It is important and has lasting impact, though its core object, dark matter, remains undetected.
assessment.attribution: Faber, White and Rees are central to the development of the CDM framework, but the credit is shared with Blumenthal, Primack, Frenk, Davis and Efstathiou, and with Peebles, who has already been recognised in 2019. The configuration is therefore not well bounded.
assessment.maturity: The paradigm is highly successful at large scales and has been tested by many surveys, but small-scale tensions and the nature of dark matter are unresolved, so a prize could be seen as either overdue or incomplete.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2019 prize and the lack of a clean, single decisive discovery.
Unsettled attribution among the many contributors to the CDM framework.
